question.text: As per SEBI regulations, what is the penalty if an AMC fails to dispatch redemption proceeds within the stipulated timeframe?

answer.text: A flat penalty of Rs. 10,000 per day of delay
Interest at the rate of 15% per annum for the period of delay
Suspension of the scheme for 30 days

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI mutual-fund regulatory framework, when an AMC fails to dispatch redemption/repurchase proceeds within the stipulated time, it must pay interest at the rate prescribed by SEBI for the period of delay — historically and as broadly cited, 15% per annum — out of the AMC's own funds rather than the scheme's assets. This protects other investors in the scheme and creates a strong operational incentive to meet the dispatch deadline. The Trap: A flat per-day rupee penalty is not how SEBI structures the delay charge — it is interest-based, not flat. Suspension of the scheme is a separate enforcement action used in serious regulatory breaches, not the standard remedy for a payout delay. Cancellation of the AMC's licence is a last-resort sanction reserved for severe, repeated, or fraudulent misconduct, not an automatic outcome of a single delayed redemption. Note: The cited workbook (NISM Series V-A — Mutual Fund Distributors, pages 171, 218, 260) supports 15% p.a. interest in the context of delayed NFO refunds, but for failure to transfer redemption/repurchase proceeds states only "interest at the rate specified by SEBI" — the 15% figure for redemption-delay specifically was not found in the cited pages. The framing above is based on the SEBI delay-interest regime as broadly published in industry references and current SEBI circulars.
